title.narrative: Improving the diet of households in rural areas in Ishkashim, Tajikistan

description.narrative: Objective: Families and households in Ishkashim improve their nutrition and food security.Goal: Households in 13 villages in the Ishkashim target area have improved their diets in terms of the principles of a balanced, nutritious diet (SDG 2).

The direct target group is approx. 500 women of child-bearing age (18-40) as well as decision-makers from their households (male heads of households, fathers-in-law, husbands), who are to be closely involved in the measures in order to increase and consolidate effects. These are achieved in particular with the PLA approach in sub-goal 1. Household members of the direct target group from sub-objective 1 also benefit from measures from sub-objective 2 and consist of approx. 1,300 men, 1,920 women, of whom approx. 200 are children under the age of 5. Direct project participants in addition are approx. 10 men and approx. 20 women from the local structures of the health system and representatives of the local civil society in sub-objective 3.Indirect project participants are all those people in the target villages who do not directly benefit from the PLA sessions or belong to their household. However, since the measures address everyone in the village and are designed to be replicated/imitated, the project will also indirectly reach 1,220 other people.

The project aims to improve food and nutrition security status of population in 13 villages in the Ishkashim region. The project follows a gender-sensitive, community-based approach involving individual households and the larger community. All activities are aimed at food and nutrition security with a special focus on dietary diversity and hygiene. To achieve the overall objective and sub-objectives, the project will apply the following proven approaches adapted to Tajikistan:(a) Nutrition-sensitive behavior change (b) Nutrition-sensitive agriculture (c) Strengthening of structuresThe reach out is planned to 3.700 direct project participants (ca. 60% of it female) and another 1.200 indirect project beneficiaries.
